correctness.rationale: For orthonormal u,v, differentiating the homogeneous quartic great-circle restriction gives Q=12a-3b-3/(d+2), a=Σu_i²v_i², b=Σu_i⁴. Minimum -3-c is attained at axes; for the maximum, 2a<=b+g, a+g<=1, a<=1-b, and a<=1/2 imply 4a-b<=3/2 by the split b<=1/2 or >=1/2, attained only at balanced signed two-coordinate normals with complementary tangent. Hence Q_max=9/2-c and support Hessian is semidefinite precisely on the stated epsilon interval. Equality analyses determine at the positive endpoint rank zero at ±e_i and at negative endpoint rank d-2 at two-coordinate normals. Positivity and differentiability of the homogeneous extension ensure strict convexity including curvature-degenerate endpoints; no assertion of positive curvature there. Independent exact-rational checks at d=3,4,5,10 reproduced thresholds and coefficient. The normalized harmonic variance 24(d-1)/[(d+2)^2(d+4)(d+6)] with Laplace eigenvalue -4(d+2) gives V/(2V)=-36d(d-1)(d+3)/[(d+2)^2(d+4)(d+6)], and determinant support-coordinate formula gives the polynomial-degree bound.
